title: Enhanced Recovery After Pediatric Cardiac Surgery – Evaluation of the Concept and Development of a Predictive Model for Early Extubation Based on Retrospective Data
summary: Congenital heart defects are the most common congenital malformations and often require one or more surgeries. As part of modern enhanced recovery concepts (ERACS), early extubation in the operating room has shown potential benefits, such as reducing intensive care unit stays and minimizing complications. However, it also carries risks, particularly if reintubation becomes necessary. This study retrospectively analyzes data to identify factors influencing the success of early extubation and patient outcomes.

interventions.name: Retrospective analysis of all patients under 18 years of age who underwent pediatric cardiac surgery at the DHZB/DHZC between January 1, 2015, and December 31, 2024.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All patients <18 years who underwent pediatric cardiac surgery at DHZB/DHZC between 01.01.2015 and 31.12.2024.
Exclusion criteria:
>18 years, tracheotomized children
